# Quiz

> Small games at https://quiz.neorgon.com/: count the beats of a loanword, pick
> the sound of a kana, match two columns, put a song line back in order. One
> JSON set per game, every wrong answer explained. Any site can embed a game
> in an iframe and read the answers back over postMessage. Nothing is uploaded.

## Writing a set file

Produce ONE JSON object in the `neo-quiz-set/1` format:

    {
      "format": "neo-quiz-set/1",
      "id": "jp-loanwords-beats",
      "version": "2026-09-04",
      "game": "beats",
      "name": { "en": "Loanword beats", "es": "Pulsos de préstamos" },
      "skill": "jp.mora.count",
      "licence": { "spdx": "CC-BY-4.0", "screen": "required",
                   "attribution": "Word list by ...", "source": "https://..." },
      "groups": { "greetings": { "en": "Greetings", "es": "Saludos" } },
      "items": [ ... ]
    }

Top-level fields:

- format (required) "neo-quiz-set/1"
- id (required) a letter or digit, then letters, digits, dot, dash or
  underscore. Scores are keyed by it, so never change it on an existing set
- version (required) a YYYY-MM-DD date, bumped on any content change
- game (required) one of beats, sound, pairs, order. A set serves one game
- name (required) a string or { "en", "es" }; "es": null means not translated
- lang (optional) BCP 47 tag of the content, default "ja"
- skill (optional) a dotted string echoed on every quiz:answer unless the URL
  gives ?skill=. With neither, the skill is "quiz.<game>"
- licence (required) { spdx (required, an SPDX id or "public-domain"), screen
  (required, "required" or "none"), attribution (the exact on-screen wording,
  required when screen is "required"), source (URL, optional) }. With screen
  "required" the attribution renders under the round on every screen that
  shows the set, the embed too, source linked beside it
- groups (optional) { "<id>": name }, name a string or { "en", "es" }: the
  words the round header shows for filter=group:<id>; an item's group is a key
- items (required) at least 1, ids unique within the set, id in the same
  character set as the set id. Shapes per game below

No field may contain markup: a "<" followed by a letter anywhere is an error.
Every learner-facing string is a bilingual value; a bare string is English.
row, column, group and rule are labels (ASCII letters, digits, dashes) that
?filter= matches exactly, never prose.

### beats

    { "id": "bag", "word": "bag", "kana": "バッグ", "romaji": "baggu",
      "beats": 3, "split": ["バ", "ッ", "グ"], "rule": "sokuon",
      "explain": { "en": "A small っ is a beat of its own, a held stop.",
                   "es": "La っ pequeña es un pulso propio, una pausa sostenida." } }

- word: the source word, shown under the kana before the answer
- kana: what is counted, shown large. romaji (required, never null) is shown
  only after the answer, because "baggu" spells out the count. Hepburn in
  macron style: a long vowel is ā ī ū ē ō (kōhī, gēmu), never oo, ou or a
  circumflex; ッ doubles the consonant after it; ン is n, n' before a vowel or y
- beats: an integer from 1 to 9 equal to split.length. The options are four
  ascending numerals around it, so a word past 9 beats needs another game
- split: the kana cut into beats; joined with "" it must equal kana
- rule: a short code naming the rule (sokuon, long-vowel, n, plain, ...), for
  set authors and the results screen; explain is its one-line human reading

### sound

    { "id": "ki", "kana": "き", "sound": "ki", "row": "k", "column": "i",
      "distractors": ["ka", "sa", "ni"] }
    { "id": "kya", "kana": "きゃ", "sound": "kya", "row": "ky", "column": "ya" }

- kana and sound: the two faces. The engine asks in either direction, chosen
  per item by seed. No two items share a sound
- row: a label shared by the kana of one row; column: "a", "i", "u", "e", "o"
  in a plain row, "ya", "yu", "yo" in a yoon row, or null (ん only). A row
  holds one kind of column and no cell twice. The feedback strip is the set's
  items sharing row, in column order: five cells for a plain row, three for a
  yoon row. Ship whole rows; a genuinely short row is not a hole (y has three)
- a yoon row is labelled by its onset as Hepburn writes it: ky, sh, ch, ny,
  hy, my, ry, gy, j, by, py. An extended katakana digraph joins its base
  kana's row when that cell is empty (ヴァ ヴィ ヴェ ヴォ beside ヴ in v), else
  opens a row named by the base's reading, plain vowel columns: fu (ファ フィ
  フェ フォ), te (ティ), to (トゥ), de, do, u (ウィ ウェ ウォ), shi (シェ), chi,
  ji, tsu (ツァ ツィ ツェ ツォ); one with a small ャュョ goes to the yoon row of
  its onset (dy: デュ). A digraph whose sound a plain kana owns is left out
- distractors (optional) sounds, 3 or more, drawn from when present; otherwise
  three sounds from the same row or the same column in the set

### pairs

    { "id": "inu", "left": "いぬ", "right": { "en": "dog", "es": "perro" },
      "note": "inu", "group": "animals" }

- left and right are the only things on the board. right is a string or
  { "en", "es" }: the board shows the reader's language, English when "es" is
  null, and says so once per screen. In either language right may not contain
  left, be contained by it or equal it after trim, casefold and strip-accents:
  that keeps the answer off the visible text. note (optional) is shown only
  in the feedback after a miss
- a board is four pairs; the set needs at least 4 items and no two rights may
  be equal after the same folding, per language
- group (optional) a key of the set's groups, what filter=group: matches. A
  kana pairs item carries row and column as its sound sibling does

### order

    { "id": "sakura-1", "tokens": ["さくら", "さくら", "野山も", "里も"],
      "line": "さくら さくら 野山も 里も",
      "gloss": { "en": "Cherry blossoms, cherry blossoms, over hills and villages",
                 "es": "Flores de cerezo, flores de cerezo, por montes y aldeas" } }

- tokens: the correct order, 3 to 9 pieces (keys 1 to 9 are the bank), no two
  equal: two pieces is a coin flip, two identical pieces have no wrong order.
  Split a longer line in two; merge a repeated piece with its neighbour
- line: the display of the correct line; equals tokens joined with "" or " "
- gloss: { "en", "es" }, shown after a miss and on the results screen, never
  before. "es": null is allowed and puts the fallback line under the surface

### Generated sets

The built-in sets are written by runcible-site/tools/build-sets.mjs from the
corpus, never by hand. Beyond the format it guarantees: a beats romaji is the
corpus's own line when it has one, else derived from the katakana through the
kana tables (ー lengthens the vowel before it, ッ doubles the consonant after
it), macron style either way, never null; a kana the tables cannot read fails
the build. A digraph's sound is derived the same way. right.es and gloss.es
are the corpus's Spanish when it has one, else null: the generator translates
nothing, and the fallback line is how a set says so.

## URL parameters

    https://quiz.neorgon.com/?game=sound&set=jp-hiragana-sound&filter=row:k&limit=10

- game=beats | sound | pairs | order. Optional when set is given: the set's
  own game is used. An unknown name is quiz:error { code: "game-unknown" };
  a set whose game differs is { code: "game-mismatch" }
- set=<id> a built-in set from data/sets/index.json, or an https URL fetched
  over CORS (http://localhost only when the engine itself is on localhost).
  Absent in embed: quiz:error { code: "no-set" }. Absent standalone: the library
- filter=<field>:<value>[,<value>...] keeps only the items whose <field>
  equals one of the values, exactly, after trim: filter=row:k, filter=row:k,s,
  filter=group:greetings. field is any item field holding a label (row,
  column, group, rule); a bilingual or numeric field never filters. An unknown
  field, an empty value list or a match of zero items is quiz:error { code:
  "filter-empty" }. limit is capped at the filtered length, the round header
  names the filter in words (the k row, the k and s rows, Greetings), "Open in
  Quiz" keeps it. Only the first filter= is read: one per round
- embed=1 strips the chrome to a slim bar whose "Open in Quiz" link keeps every
  other parameter (filter included) except embed and skill; the round starts on load
- limit=<N> items per round, default 10, capped at the set's length. A value
  that is not a finite positive integer is discarded
- seed=<string> makes the shuffle, the numeral window and the sound direction
  deterministic, so a host can replay a round. Default: random per load
- lang=en | es. Absent: the saved preference, then the browser, then en
- skill=<dotted> overrides the set's skill on every quiz:answer
- theme=<name> is read by the fleet's pre-paint theme script, as on every site

## Embedding (iframe), contract `neo-quiz-embed/1`

    <iframe src="https://quiz.neorgon.com/?embed=1&game=beats&limit=10&set=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fbeats.json"
      width="100%" height="560" loading="lazy" style="border:0"
      title="Loanword beats · Quiz"></iframe>

### Messages the engine sends you

Every message is `{ v: 1, type, ... }`, posted to your origin (the referrer's),
never `*`; with no referrer the engine posts nothing. **Ignore any message
whose `v` you do not recognise.** chosen and expected are always strings.

- quiz:ready `{ setId, setVersion, game, name, total, store }`. total is the
  round length after filter and limit; store is "engine" when this frame
  writes quiz:scores:v1, else "ephemeral" (see the allowlist). Fires once the
  set resolved, and again every time you send quiz:hello
- quiz:answer `{ setId, game, itemId, skill, correct, ms, chosen, expected }`,
  one per item; in pairs one per pair, decided by the first attempt on that
  left item. ms runs from the item's first paint (in pairs, the previous
  lock) to the commit
- quiz:session-end `{ setId, game, answered, correct, wrong, ms, medianMs,
  bestStreak, total, complete }`, once per round, as the results screen
  renders. complete is false when the learner left early (embed only: Leave
  shows partial results and records no score); a host marking an exercise
  finished checks it first
- quiz:error `{ code, message }`. Codes: no-set, set-fetch-failed,
  set-invalid, game-unknown, game-mismatch, filter-empty. The frame shows its
  own message either way; this lets you fall back
- quiz:resize `{ height }`, debounced 120ms. Clamp it; the frame does not

**If you stop receiving quiz:answer, nothing looks broken.** The frame keeps
showing a working game and you quietly stop recording: that is why every
message carries a version, and why silence after quiz:ready is a fault.

### Messages you can send the engine

Every inbound message must carry `v: 1` and a `type` starting with `quiz:`;
anything else is dropped. All three are accepted from any origin: they are
read-only or round-scoped.

- quiz:hello `{ v: 1 }`. The engine re-emits quiz:ready. **Send this on the
  iframe's load event**: the engine can be ready before your listener exists
- quiz:start `{ limit?, seed? }`. Starts or restarts a round
- quiz:theme `{ theme }`, up to 32 letters, digits, `_` or `-`, applied to documentElement.dataset.theme

    const QUIZ = 'https://quiz.neorgon.com';
    window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
      if (e.origin !== QUIZ || e.source !== frame.contentWindow) return;
      const m = e.data; if (!m || m.v !== 1) return;
      if (m.type === 'quiz:answer') record(m.itemId, m.skill, m.correct, m.ms);
    });
    frame.addEventListener('load', () => frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ v: 1, type: 'quiz:hello' }, QUIZ));

### The origin allowlist, and the one invariant

Nothing a host can send writes storage, so the allowlist decides one thing:
whether an embedded frame persists at all. At boot the engine takes the
referrer's origin and asks

    allowed(origin, self) =
         origin === "https://neorgon.com"
      || origin ends with ".neorgon.com" over https      // label boundary, not substring
      || (self and origin are both http://localhost:* or http://127.0.0.1:*)

An allowed host gets store "engine": the round is written to quiz:scores:v1
on quiz.neorgon.com, so a game played inside runcible.neorgon.com shows up in
the library's last score (same-site only: browsers partition third-party
storage by top-level site, Safari may partition even this). Any other host,
or no referrer, gets "ephemeral": nothing is written, and "Open in Quiz" is
the path that always persists.

**The invariant, stated once: an unlisted origin can never cause a write to
quiz.neorgon.com's persistent storage.** The localhost clause is gated on the
engine itself being local, dead code in production; it exists so that
http://localhost:8878 (Runcible) can embed http://localhost:8880 (Quiz) for
real. It is a pure function, `isAllowedOrigin(origin, selfOrigin)` in
js/origin.js, from rappel-site with the label-boundary check, and
tools/test-origin.mjs covers Rappel's cases: lookalikes (evil-neorgon.com,
neorgon.com.evil.io, xneorgon.com, a trailing dot), the apex over http, "null",
"", a URL with a path, query or credentials, file:, data:, javascript:,
undefined and a non-string all refused; localhost:8878 allowed only when self
is localhost:8880, never https://localhost, localhost.evil.io or a LAN address.
The same file carries isAllowedSetSrc and namespacedSetId (the ext: rule).

## The game module interface

Every game is one ES module in js/games/<id>.js, under 500 lines, exporting
`{ id, name, describe, keys, mount(host, round, api) }`; mount returns `{ destroy() }`.

- id equals the file name and the set's game; name and describe, bilingual,
  are what the library and the round header show
- keys lists the keys the module binds beyond the digits (order: ["Backspace"]),
  listed in the ? sheet, refused if reserved (?, h, g). The module adds its
  own listener and removes it in destroy(); digits are the engine's
- mount is called once per item with host emptied. round is
  { items, index, lang, embed, pool }: items the shuffled, filtered round,
  index the first item not yet answered, lang "en" or "es", embed a boolean,
  pool every item of the set (the row strip and the distractors draw from it,
  so a filter on one row still shows the whole row). pairs takes four from index
- api is { answer, next, say, t }: answer({ itemId, correct, ms, chosen,
  expected, why? }) records one verdict and posts quiz:answer, why being
  { text, node? }, text the one sentence the results screen and live region
  read, node the rich explanation the panel shows (tiles, the row strip, the
  marked line); a wrong answer without why is a defect the engine logs.
  next() says the mount is done: the engine shows the panel for every wrong
  answer since this mount and advances on Continue, or after 600ms when there
  were none; modules never advance themselves. say(text) writes to the polite
  live region. t(obj, vars?) resolves a bilingual value by round.lang with
  English fallback and fills {name} placeholders
- options are <button type="button" data-key="N">: the engine binds digits 1
  to 9 and clicks the matching data-key; keycap(n) from js/ui.js renders the
  box beside it, the digit never in the button's text. beats renders no
  keycaps: each numeral tile's data-key is its own value

## Storage

- quiz:prefs:v1 `{ v: 1, lang: "en" | "es", round: 5 | 10 | 20, lastGame: <game> | null }`
- quiz:scores:v1 `{ v: 1, rounds: { "<game>/<setId>": { played, last: { correct,
  total, at }, best: { correct, total }, bestStreak } } }`, at in ms. A
  filtered round is keyed like the whole set: a filter is not a second score
- a set fetched from an origin other than neorgon.com or a subdomain is keyed
  `ext:<first 12 hex of SHA-256 of the URL>:<id>`, so a third-party document
  claiming a built-in id cannot merge into it; `setId` carries that key
- neither is written in an ephemeral frame; both are read defensively, and a
  document with another v is ignored, not migrated

## Runcible: the quiz exercise

    { "id": "e-sound-k", "type": "quiz", "game": "sound", "skill": "jp.kana.hiragana.sound",
      "src": "books/japanese/sets/jp-hiragana-sound.json", "limit": 10,
      "filter": "row:k", "title": { "en": "The k row" } }

- type "quiz" with game (required, one of the four), src (required), skill
  (required), limit (optional positive integer), filter (optional, the URL
  grammar, one field; validate-book checks the grammar and that src carries a
  matching item, so filter-empty is a build error, never a learner's screen)
- src is a neo-quiz-set/1 document on Runcible's origin and MUST be declared
  in the Book's data[]; an undeclared src is a load error, the deck's rule
- skill is what the host records: every quiz:answer becomes one attempt
  { itemId, skill: spec.skill, correct, ms, answer: chosen, expected }, source
  "quiz". The engine's skill is informational. The deck rule applies
  unchanged: a skill nothing in the Book reads is an error
- the host builds ?embed=1&game=&set=<absolute src>&skill=&lang=&limit=&filter=
  at the engine origin (https://quiz.neorgon.com, or http://localhost:8880 when
  the host is local), sends quiz:hello on load, filters on e.origin and
  e.source, drops unknown v, converts session-end into api.done, shouts a
  malformed answer on the page, times eight seconds of silence, and renders an
  "Open in Quiz" link beside the exercise, filter kept, frame loaded or not

## Keyboard

1 to 9 answer. Space or Enter continues. Backspace undoes a piece in order. Esc
asks before leaving a round; R restarts it. `?` sheet, `H` chrome (standalone only), `G` fleet switcher.
